_comment: SECRETS TEMPLATE. Copy this file to config.local.json (which is gitignored) and fill in your Telegram bot token + chat id. config.local.json values override config.json. Never commit real secrets.
_tg_control_comment: Set tg_control_enabled=true to ARM the Telegram inline-button mode-switcher (a tap drives a flipped session back to bypass/auto via OS keystrokes). Off by default. SINGLE CONSUMER: enable on exactly ONE machine (the one whose Windows Terminal hosts the sessions), else Telegram getUpdates returns 409 and the loser self-demotes PERMANENTLY. Only telegram_chat_id is authorized to trigger.
_spoke_comment: SECOND MACHINE? Both keys below live in the tracked config.json, NOT here — this file's JSON errors are swallowed silently, and a security flag that can silently revert to 'on' is not a security flag. Set `local_machine` to this box's key in the machines registry so its rows are distinguishable in the dashboard and in every push. Set `alerts_enabled: false` on any box that must not push outward — e.g. a work machine whose real repo names must not reach Telegram. Do NOT rely on 'just don't fill in the bot token': copying this file to a second machine brings the token (and tg_control_enabled) with it. Boundary: alerts_enabled does NOT stop office_push.py (separate process, pushes pseudonymised names by design), does NOT stop the office relay pull (inbound only), and does NOT stop LAN exposure via bind_host.
_office_comment: Office relay. office_secret = shared HMAC key (secrets.token_hex(32)), SAME value on the pushing machine and here. office_ntfy_topic = a long random ntfy topic (secrets.token_urlsafe(24)) used as a bearer secret. Both flat/top-level.
